Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-cdebc5f1 — boundary bars, marker rays, and projected lines (partially solved; exact behavior variant-dependent)

## New recurrence: accepted test (14x18, 2026-10-21)
Input background 8; top boundary bar color 2 at row 0, columns 16–17; bottom bar color 2 at row 13, columns 5–6; color-5 markers at (r2,c6) and (r6,c5). Accepted output:
- Preserve both bars.
- Paint color 5 down column 16 for rows 1–13 inclusive (including cell r13,c16 despite bottom bar elsewhere).
- Paint color 5 in columns 16 and 17 for rows 1–13 inclusive (important: accepted output has BOTH columns filled; earlier tries with c16 only were wrong).
- Paint color 5 up column 6 on rows 3–12; convert marker (r2,c6) to 4. Leave marker (r6,c5) unchanged.
- Other cells remain background 8.
The accepted output had rows 1–13 col16=5 and col17=5, plus col6=5 for rows 3–12, with r2c6=4; original r6c5 stays 5. This succeeded on the eighth submission after seven wrong attempts and seven demo requests. The key correction was including BOTH cells of the top bar (c16,c17) as full vertical projections, not a single “central” lane, and only the bottom projection at c6 matching the marker; do not fill c5. This exact test/output is strong evidence but does not explain why analogous two-cell bars in demo3 appeared to emit only a single lane; fresh examples should resolve this apparent inconsistency.

## High-confidence evidence
The test (21x27) was confirmed **CORRECT** by the environment. Background was 8. Two opposite-side bars of color 9: left bar at column 0, rows 4–11; right bar at column 26, rows 13–20. Six isolated color-3 markers in the interior at zero-based coordinates:
`(4,17), (6,21), (7,2), (9,22), (10,5), (11,17)`.

Accepted output behavior:
1. Each input marker becomes color 4.
2. On the marker's own row, paint color 3 from the left bar's inner side (column 1) through the cell immediately before the marker. Do not paint beyond the marker on that row. Thus segments are r4 c1–16; r6 c1–20; r7 c1; r9 c1–21; r10 c1–4; r11 c1–16; marker itself is 4.
3. Also project each marker's position along the left bar's 8-row span onto the opposing right bar's 8-row span. Left span starts at r4, right at r13: map `r -> r+9`. For each mapped row, color the full interior between bars (columns 0–25) with 3, retaining the right-bar cells at c26 as 9. Mapped rows are r13, r15, r16, r18, r19, r20. Other rows 13–20 remain background 8 except the right border.
4. Preserve all other cells and dimensions.

This exact output was accepted after multiple earlier wrong submissions. The correct distinction is that there are both short rays from the left bar to each marker and full-width projected stripes at the matching slot on the opposite bar. It is not simply a full stripe on the marker's row, and marker row is offset by 9 for the opposite-bar projection.

## Demos and general task-family clue
- Repeated demos show a plain background, matching colored boundary bars on opposite edges (horizontal or vertical orientations), isolated interior marker(s) in another color, and output rays/projections. Markers are recolored to 4; beam/projection cells use the marker's original color. Preserve bar colors, background elsewhere, and grid size.
- In horizontal examples, bars at top/bottom were separated by a positional offset. A marker's coordinate along one bar span maps by its relative offset to the opposing bar span, creating a perpendicular stripe/beam; the marker also extends a same-row/column ray toward the nearby bar. For example demo 2 (22x15) had top bar color2 c0–2 and bottom bar color2 c5–7; input color8 markers at (13,7),(17,5),(19,6). Output filled top-aligned columns c2,c0,c1 respectively (rows1–20) in 8, converted markers to 4, and extended each marker downward to just before bottom bar in color8.
- Demo 4 (14x12) had color8 bars at top c9–11 and bottom c6–8, background7; markers color2 at (1,6),(11,7),(11,8). Output projected the top bar's corresponding lanes downward in color2, extended markers toward the bottom bar, and recolored markers 4.
- Treat the side/orientation and each bar span's offset carefully; map by index within the corresponding source span, not absolute row/column. Rays stop at the boundary and output stripe rows/columns are determined by relative position along the boundary segment.

## Common failure modes observed
Several guesses incorrectly painted marker rows all the way across to the opposite boundary, or filled the wrong half of the grid. For the accepted vertical test, only the marker-to-left-bar ray uses the marker's own row; the full-width stripe is on the *opposite-bar row* at the matching relative index. Keep the border cell colors unchanged and change each marker to 4.
